Aeromys.distinguishing_notes: Largest flying squirrel genus in the group (HB c. 255-426 mm; HMW, ADW/Nowak). Separated from the other genera here by its cylindrical, non-distichous tail whose base is enclosed in a well-developed interfemoral membrane (Robinson & Kloss 1915; Ellerman 1940), naked soles except heel (Robinson & Kloss 1915), untufted naked ears (Li et al. 2021; HMW) and bullae with three incomplete septa (McKenna 1962; Li et al. 2021 '<4'). Versus Petaurista (also large, round-tailed; not in this group) Robinson & Kloss and Ellerman use the Hylopetes-like (Sciuropterus-group) cheekteeth. Caveat: large Philippine Petinomys (P. mindanensis 320-370 mm, 'more rounded rather than flattened tail') overlap in size and tail shape but do not co-occur with Aeromys; Sundaic P. hageni (230-313 mm) overlaps in size, so size alone is insufficient - use tail/interfemoral membrane and bullar septa.

Hylopetes.distinguishing_notes: Medium-small to medium flying squirrels (HB c.100-330 mm) with a broad feather-shaped tail (Ellerman 1940; indistinctly so in H. nigripes and H. bartelsi). Versus Iomys: Hylopetes has P3 (5 upper cheekteeth) and non-quadricuspidate molars; Iomys lacks P3 and has square, quadricuspidate molars (Thomas 1908; Ellerman 1940; Li et al. 2021) - but H. winstoni (originally Iomys) is unverified. Versus Petinomys: best sourced separator is the internal bullar septa (Hylopetes two/<4 simple septa vs Petinomys complex 'honeycomb'/cobweb septa; McKenna 1962; Li et al. 2021), plus baculum shape (Pocock 1923 via McKenna 1962: single crest, apex simple vs supplementary crest, apex spatulate). Thomas's (1908) inflated-vs-flat bullae fails for H. electilis and H. bartelsi; P. setosus has been reported with only five septa (Kruskop et al. 2022, syntype) so the septa character is imperfect for small Petinomys. Molecular data show Hylopetes paraphyletic with respect to Petinomys (Kruskop et al. 2022). Versus Olisthomys: Olisthomys has unsculptured teeth and low spreading bullae with about six septa (Carter 1942; McKenna 1962; Kruskop et al. 2022). Versus Pteromyscus: Pteromyscus has excessively wrinkled Belomys-like molars, minute P3 and much inflated bullae (Thomas 1908; Ellerman 1940). Versus Petaurillus: Petaurillus is tiny (HB <=96 mm) with P4 decidedly smaller than M1. Versus Aeromys: Aeromys has a round non-distichous tail and well-developed interfemoral membrane.

Olisthomys.distinguishing_notes: Small flying squirrel (HB c.115-135 mm in measured specimens) formerly treated as 'northern' Petinomys setosus. Diagnosed by Carter (1942) as near Hylopetes 'but without any sculpturing on the teeth and with the low spreading bullae of Petinomys'; McKenna (1962) and Kruskop et al. (2022) add about six simple bullar septa (vs two/<4 in Hylopetes and complex honeycomb/cobweb septa in Petinomys). Versus true P. setosus Kruskop et al. (2022) list cranial differences from the syntype (nasofrontal suture nearly transverse vs W-shaped; coronal suture transverse vs V-shaped; interorbital/postorbital width ratio 0.64 vs 0.77) but these rest on n=1 vs n=1; the P. setosus syntype also has few (five) septa. HMW says northern specimens are marginally larger and usually white-tipped, but ADW (Sanamxay et al. 2019 data) reports Lao specimens lacking the white tail tip, so tail tip colour is unreliable. NO robust external character separating Olisthomys from small Petinomys (setosus, vordermanni) was found; the Olisthomys/Petinomys pair is effectively separable only by skull/teeth.

Petaurillus.distinguishing_notes: Pygmy flying squirrels: HB 68-96 mm, body mass <50 g (Li et al. 2021 key). Dental diagnosis: P4 decidedly smaller than M1 with a well-developed P3, so the three anterior cheekteeth decrease evenly in size; molar ridges low and rounded, not wrinkled (Thomas 1908; Ellerman 1940). CAUTION on size: the smallest Petinomys (P. setosus HB 92-128 mm, P. vordermanni 92-120 mm, HMW) and Olisthomys overlap Petaurillus at 92-96 mm, and their weights (22-58 g) overlap Petaurillus kinlochii (17-31 g); use P4<M1 (and bullar septa: Petaurillus <4 vs >4 in Petinomys and Olisthomys; Li et al. 2021 Table S6) to separate. P3 is occasionally absent in Petaurillus (Li et al. 2021 'mostly P'), so premolar count does not cleanly separate it from Iomys; Iomys is much larger (HB >=165 mm) with quadricuspidate molars.

cheekteeth_excessively_wrinkled.notes: Ellerman 1940 primary key split: cheekteeth with extreme complication due to wrinkling, pattern masked (Trogopterus, Belomys, Pteromyscus, Petaurista) vs 'a more normal pattern, the wrinkling ... never excessive' (Petaurillus, Iomys, Aeromys, Petinomys, Pteromys, Glaucomys, Eoglaucomys, Hylopetes); Thomas 1908 key: 'Teeth excessively wrinkled' with an outwardly projecting angle on the outer edge (Trogopterus, Belomys, Pteromyscus) vs 'not excessively wrinkled. No projecting angle' (Sciuropterus s.l. incl. Hylopetes, Petinomys and the species now in Aeromys; Petaurillus). Petinomys enamel is 'elaborately sculptured' (Thomas 1908) but not of the excessively wrinkled, pattern-masking Belomys/Pteromyscus type.

Petinomys.distinguishing_notes: Very wide size range (HB 92-370 mm). Best-sourced generic characters: bullae low and flattened with thick opaque walls (Thomas 1908; weaker in P. fuscocapillus) and internal bullar septa complex 'honeycomb'/cobweb-like (McKenna 1962; Li et al. 2021 key), molar enamel elaborately sculptured with strong mesostyle/mesoloph, and baculum with supplementary crest and spatulate apex (Pocock 1923 via McKenna 1962). Versus Hylopetes: septa (complex vs two/<4) - but the P. setosus syntype has only five septa (Kruskop et al. 2022), and bulla flattening also occurs in Hylopetes electilis and H. bartelsi, so small species are difficult; molecular data show Hylopetes paraphyletic relative to Petinomys. Versus Pteromyscus (sizes overlap): Petinomys has no distinct hypocone (Li et al. 2021 key couplet 1; McKenna 1962) and its cheekteeth are not of the excessively wrinkled Belomys type (Ellerman 1940; Thomas 1908), whereas Pteromyscus has a distinct hypocone, excessively wrinkled molars with an outer projecting angle and small untufted ears. Versus Iomys: P3 present, molars not quadricuspidate. Versus Petaurillus: P4 not smaller than M1 (sizes overlap at 92-96 mm). Versus Aeromys: no well-developed interfemoral membrane; but large P. mindanensis has a 'more rounded' tail. Versus Olisthomys: sculptured molars and complex septa vs smooth teeth and about six simple septa; no reliable external separator found. Several species have long tufts around the ears and cheek 'whiskers' (genibarbis, crinitus, mindanensis, hageni, lugens).

Pteromyscus.distinguishing_notes: Medium-large (HB 200-290 mm). Generic characters: Belomys/Trogopterus-like excessively wrinkled cheekteeth with a projecting angle on the outer edge (less marked than Belomys), P3 minute/vestigial, P4 about equal to or slightly smaller than M1, bullae much inflated with narrowed basioccipital, ears small and untufted (Thomas 1908; Ellerman 1940); about five bullar septa (Li et al. 2021). Versus Iomys (similar size): Pteromyscus usually has a minute P3 (absent in a few individuals; Li et al. 2021 'mostly P') and wrinkled, non-quadricuspidate molars, and >4 honeycomb bullar septa vs <4 in Iomys. Versus Hylopetes/Petinomys: much more complex (wrinkled) molars, much inflated bullae, small untufted ears; pelage dark, 'frosted'/flecked with white. Versus Aeromys: smaller, no well-developed interfemoral membrane. Versus Belomys (co-occurs in Thailand): ears small and untufted vs large and tufted; P4 not enlarged. Li et al. 2021 key: Pteromyscus has a distinct hypocone on the upper cheekteeth (couplet 1b), unlike Hylopetes, Petinomys and Petaurillus (1a).

caveats: 1) Composition changes matter: under MDD v2.5 Hylopetes includes bartelsi and electilis (described in Petinomys, with low/flattened Petinomys-type bullae), winstoni (described in Iomys) and sipora; Olisthomys morrisi is split from Petinomys setosus. Classic genus diagnoses (Thomas 1908, Ellerman 1940) were written for older compositions; scope fields flag where species are not covered. 2) Hylopetes winstoni is known from one specimen; no dental description was retrieved, so whether it has P3 (Hylopetes) or lacks it (Iomys-like) is unverified - Hylopetes upper_premolars is therefore 'partial'. ADW also (probably erroneously) gives one upper premolar for H. spadiceus. 3) Pteromyscus P3 is minute and 'often hardly visible from above' (Thomas 1908), and Li et al. 2021 Table S6 scores both Pteromyscus and Petaurillus P3 as 'mostly P' (absent in a few individuals), so both genera are recorded as ['1','2']; only Iomys consistently lacks P3. 4) Ear tufts: Hylopetes (bartelsi, winstoni), Petinomys (crinitus, mindanensis, hageni, genibarbis) and Olisthomys have long tufts/bristles at the BASE of the ear or on the cheek, not ear-tip pencils; 'present' was added for safety. 5) flank_stripe left unknown everywhere because pale/dark patagium margins are routinely described and could be read as flank stripes. dorsal_stripes, dorsal_spots, tail_rings, cheek_pouches, upper_incisor_groove and (except Aeromys) hairy_soles are mostly unknown because no retrieved source states them; absence is likely for most but was not sourced. 6) Quotes from Thomas 1908, Ellerman 1940, Robinson & Kloss 1915 and Chasen 1939 are verbatim from OCR text, including OCR errors (e.g. 'p*', 'p°', 'p^' for superscript premolar numbers, 'Bulle'/'Bullee' for Bullae, "Cheekteeth 'i" for cheekteeth 5/4). HMW quotes come from Plazi OCR, where decimal points appear as hyphens ('375-4' = 375.4). 7) hb_length for Olisthomys is the P. setosus sensu lato envelope (92-140), because no range for O. morrisi alone was retrievable; measured individuals are 115 (Kruskop et al. 2022) and 135 (Carter 1942 holotype, by subtraction). 8) Li et al. 2021's Supplementary Materials were recovered from a truncated Europe PMC zip (PDF missing its last ~8 kB/xref); text was decoded from the PDF content streams with the embedded ToUnicode maps, so table quotes contain decoder spacing artefacts ('P etinomys', 'm ostly'); the table row order/columns were checked against the header and legend. Li et al. treated Olisthomys within P. setosus (their sample includes the Olisthomys holotype AMNH 113031) and examined H. bartelsi only as a skull and H. sipora only as a skin. Jackson & Thorington 2012 (SCZ 638) is a nomenclatural catalogue with no morphological diagnoses for these genera.
